Today's Featured Research Reports

Tesla's shares have outperformed the Zacks Automotive - Domestic industry over the past six months (+9.3% vs. +9.1%). The company's vehicle backlog, rising FSD subscriptions and expanding Robotaxi fleet strengthen its long-term software and mobility prospects. Demand for energy storage, supported by data center expansion and new Megapack capacity, adds another growth avenue. 

Charging, insurance and other services revenues also diversify its business. Cash generation and liquidity provide flexibility to fund these initiatives. However, lower vehicle selling prices, declining regulatory credit revenues and rising operating expenses pressure profitability and near-term earnings. 

Heavy investments in AI, robotics and manufacturing could constrain free cash flow. Battery supply limitations and regulatory hurdles add execution risks, while a stretched valuation leaves limited room for setbacks. Thus, the stock warrants a cautious stance now. 

(You can read the full research report on Tesla here >>>)

Shares of Netflix have underperformed the Zacks Broadcast Radio and Television industry over the past six months (-32.1% vs. -25.8%). The company's 2026 advertising outlook was cut to about $2.7 billion from roughly $3 billion, and fourth-quarter margin is guided to 26% due to headcount reductions. Competition for viewing time remains intense. Content obligations of $25.2 billion, gross debt of $15.3 billion and record buybacks demand continued cash discipline.

Nevertheless, Netflix's investment case remains balanced. Third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 12% to $12.87 billion, in line with forecast, while operating margin expanded to 34.6% from 28.2%, helped by expense timing. Management expects full-year 2026 revenue of about $51.1 billion, up 13%, with operating margin of 31.5% and free cash flow of roughly $12 billion. 

Pricing, improved churn and a global audience approaching one billion people support the subscription engine, while partnerships with TF1 and Disney broaden content. 

(You can read the full research report on Netflix here >>>)

American Express' shares have declined -0.3% over the past six months against the Zacks Financial - Miscellaneous Services industry's decline of -6.6%. The company's expenses rose 11% YoY in the first nine months, outpacing revenue growth and reflecting higher customer engagement and operating costs. Credit performance remains strong, but macroeconomic pressures could affect spending and credit costs. A sizable debt burden and regulatory uncertainty add risks.

Nevertheless, American Express' third-quarter earnings beat estimates. It benefits from its differentiated Membership Model, strong Card Member spending and sustained customer acquisition, particularly among Millennials and Gen Z. 

Travel, dining, partnerships and digital initiatives are enhancing its differentiated premium customer value proposition. The proposed TheFork acquisition could expand its lifestyle ecosystem and international reach. In the first nine months of 2026, total revenues grew 10% YoY. 

(You can read the full research report on American Express here >>>)

Shares of InterGroup have declined -17.5% over the past six months against the Zacks Real Estate - Development industry's decline of -24.9%. This microcap company with a market capitalization of $74.84 million is facing substantial debt, approaching loan maturities, rising financing costs and refinancing uncertainty -- all of which pose significant risks. Restricted cash availability and declining operating cash flow further constrain flexibility. Dependence on a single hotel, rising labor costs and rent regulations could pressure margins. Valuation discounts to industry on EV/sales basis. 

Nevertheless, InterGroup's improving hotel demand, stronger room pricing and higher occupancy supported a return to profitability in fiscal 2026. Rising operating income, lower mortgage interest expenses and stronger rental margins further supported earnings. 

Hotel renovations, additional guestrooms, its Hilton affiliation and a favorable location enhance competitive positioning and revenue potential. Its diversified rental portfolio provides stable income, while disciplined cost management and strategic asset sales strengthen financial flexibility and support debt reduction. 

(You can read the full research report on InterGroup here >>>)

Moving iMage Technologies' shares have underperformed the Zacks Technology Services industry over the past six months (-17.9% vs. -14.1%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $5.20 million is facing persistent revenue declines. Project delays are weakening its growth visibility. Negative operating cash flow, declining cash reserves and elevated inventory risks could constrain investments. 

Shrinking backlog adds uncertainty to future revenues, while slow commercialization of emerging technologies limits diversification. The stock trades at a discount to industry peers on EV/sales basis. Nevertheless, MiT benefits from the DCS acquisition, which expands its proprietary offerings and global reach. Integrated cinema solutions create cross-selling opportunities and encourage repeat business. 

Recent theater upgrades demonstrate its product breadth and ability to address diverse customer requirements. A diversified customer base limits concentration risks, while its debt-free balance sheet provides financial flexibility. International expansion and stronger dealer relationships could support sustained demand. 

(You can read the full research report on Moving iMage Technologies here >>>)

title: Elon Musk Says Neoclouds Face a "Guppy Level" Death. IREN Is Down 64% From Its High. Is He Talking About This Stock?
detail:
Elon Musk Says Neoclouds Face a "Guppy Level" Death. IREN Is Down 64% From Its High. Is He Talking About This Stock?
Leo Sun, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 4:15 PM EDT 4 min read
IREN
SPCX
NVDA
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Tesla CEO Elon Musk recently posted on X that over the past few weeks, debt markets have "almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers". Musk believes that tightening could cause more than 200 neocloud companies -- which mainly provide AI infrastructure services -- to face a "guppy-level death and consolidation" in the near future.

That statement caused many neocloud stocks to plummet. One of the hardest-hit stocks was IREN (NASDAQ: IREN), which trades 64% below its all-time high from last November. Let's see why a tightening debt market could spell trouble for this former market darling.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
What could happen to IREN?

IREN was once an Australian Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) miner called Iris Energy. In 2024, it rebranded as IREN and became a neocloud AI infrastructure company. As IREN, the company allocated all of its capital, logistics, and power infrastructure toward expanding its AI and high-performance computing (HPC) data centers rather than its Bitcoin mining operations.

Today, IREN has a fleet of six operational data centers across four countries. It plans to bring seven additional data centers online in the near future. It plans to increase its capacity from 810 MW today to 4.5 GW over the long term. Its 2026 capacity is already "largely" sold out, and it's in "late-stage discussions" with new customers for a "significant portion" of its 2027 capacity.

IREN has already secured multi-billion-dollar cloud services contracts with Microsoft, Nvidia, and other AI giants. It requires many of those customers to prepay roughly half of the GPU capex, reducing its upfront capital requirements.

From fiscal 2026 (which ended in June) to fiscal 2029, analysts expect its revenue and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) to grow at CAGRs of 177% and 243%, respectively, as it expands its capacity and converts its backlog into revenue.

With an enterprise value of $34.6 billion, IREN trades at just 12 times this year's sales and 19 times its adjusted EBITDA. However, its net losses -- which include interest payments, hardware depreciation, and stock-based compensation excluded from its adjusted EBITDA -- are expected to widen from $703 million in fiscal 2026 to $1.05 billion in fiscal 2029.

title: 2 AI Stocks to Buy if the Market Sells Off Before Year-End
detail:
2 AI Stocks to Buy if the Market Sells Off Before Year-End
Prosper Junior Bakiny, The Motley Fool
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 3:57 PM EDT 5 min read
SPCX
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The broader stock market has been resilient this year despite significant problems, including geopolitical tensions and a challenging macroeconomic landscape. However, it is still possible that equities will experience a sell-off by the end of the year. Long-term investors need not worry too much about that. Stock market downturns happen fairly regularly, and they typically offer astute investors the opportunity to pick up shares of great companies on the dip.

And with many people fearing that the market is overvalued right now due to pricey artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, a sell-off might make some AI companies much more attractive. With that said, let's consider two AI stocks to buy if there is a market downturn by year-end: Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
1. Space Exploration Technologies

According to management, SpaceX could generate $1 trillion in revenue by 2030, with AI accounting for 99% of the company's value by then. Those are ambitious goals, but they might be within SpaceX's reach after all. The company has added several AI compute deals to its portfolio in recent months, and its AI segment has been its fastest-growing.

In the third quarter, SpaceX's total revenue increased by 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. The company's AI segment, dubbed Super Intelligence (SI), recorded $7.6 billion in sales, up 830% compared to the year-ago period. That wasn't all organic growth, but even putting aside an acquisition that closed in August and contributed $608 million in revenue for SI, the segment's year-over-year sales growth was an impressive 755%.

What's more, SpaceX still sees significant demand ahead for its AI products. CEO Elon Musk said we may be moving toward a shortage of SI compute that could last a while. There is some evidence for that from SpaceX's own business. The company is seeing several times as much demand for AI compute as it is willing to rent out, and even older systems are renting at a premium compared to when they were new.

If this trend continues, SpaceX's SI business could maintain strong revenue growth over the medium term. However, the market seems to have already factored that into the share price. SpaceX's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 85.5, which is very high. And despite significant progress across all three of its segments since its debut on equity markets -- as well as excellent financial results -- the stock hasn't gained much, if at all. SpaceX is a great business and would be much more attractive at the right price. It could reach that price if a sell-off is imminent. But at current levels, the stock isn't a buy.

Tesla Gains Another 4% as ARK Restates $4,400 Robotaxi Target and Musk Teases "A Storm of Cybercabs" ©DOD photo via Canva
Key Takeaways

Tesla shares rose 4% today, adding to Monday's gain on a Barclays upgrade, after ARK Invest restated its $4,400 price target for 2031.

Barclays' $450 target rests on a SpaceX merger, while ARK puts about 80% of Tesla's 2031 value on robotaxis.

Tesla trades far above its five-year average forward P/E, but consensus estimates through 2028 show little profit from robotaxis yet.

Tesla's factory can now build Cybercabs faster than it can put them into service. Next up are the Dallas launch in November and the first real robotaxi revenue in 2027.

Tesla (TSLA:NASDAQ) is up 4% today, adding to Monday's rally on a Barclays upgrade. After Monday's close, ARK Invest's Tasha Keeney restated the firm's $4,400 base-case target for 2031.

Overnight, Elon Musk posted on X: "A Storm of Cybercabs."

That's two bulls in two days, making very different bets.

Two targets, two stories

Barclays analyst Dan Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight and raised his target to $450 from $370. "We believe the anticipated merger is now a key part of the Tesla bull case," the analysts wrote, meaning a deal with SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ). Tesla and SpaceX have each formed special committees, and no terms have been set.

ARK's case rests on robotaxis. Its model, updated Oct. 19, ties about 80% of Tesla's 2031 enterprise value to them: about 8.1 million robotaxis bringing in $753 billion of net ride-hail revenue that year.

The rest of Wall Street sits much closer to Barclays. The consensus target has climbed to $411 from $386 a year ago, and the highest is $600.

Tesla (TSLA): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

ARK's $4,400 is more than 7x even that high.

The stock is already pricing robotaxis

Tesla traded at 183x forward earnings at Monday's close, against a five-year average of 108x, and today's gain pushes it closer to 190x:

Tesla (TSLA): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Yet consensus estimates show little of a robotaxi business. Normalized EPS is expected to climb from $1.66 in 2025 to $3.20 in 2028, still below the $4.07 Tesla earned in 2022.

Tesla (TSLA): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)

Closing that gap takes robotaxi profits, and a merger premium won't supply them.

TIKR tracks 44 analysts on Tesla. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Tesla, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Tesla's Analyst Ratings

Building them is the easy part

Musk's post lands as Tesla says its Texas Cybercab factory can now build robotaxis faster than it can put them into service, so the line doesn't need to run every day.

Cybertruck in a parking lot (Credit: Photo: wedmoments.stock / Shutterstock.com)
Chris Katje

The Tesla Inc Cybertruck has significantly underperformed compared to initial projections set by CEO Elon Musk. Recent quarterly results show dismal numbers, and things could get worse for the company's unique-looking electric pickup truck.

Tesla Cancels Cybertruck Orders

The Cybertruck was only available for residents of the U.S. for many years. Consumers in other markets who wanted the EV truck have had to reserve their place in line for the eventual launch in more international territories.

Excited reservation holders in Australia and New Zealand recently had their hopes crushed.

The EV company has canceled selling the vehicle in those two countries, sending out emails to let reservation holders know that they will be refunded, as reported by Electrek.

Dating back to 2019, residents in the country could reserve a Cybertruck with 150 Australian Dollars.

"After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued. As a result, we're unable to fulfill your reservation and it will be cancelled," an email reads, according to the report.

Along with a refund of any payments made, reservation holders in the countries are being offered a free one-year subscription for FSD if they buy a new Model Y or Model 3.

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

What's Next for Cybertruck?

Tesla emailed residents in Australia and New Zealand a day after the company reported third-quarter financial results. While that timing could have been coincidental, it also begs the question of if it was done to try and bury the news.

Australia has been a strong market for Tesla vehicles in 2026, but those vehicles are made in China and ship faster than a Cybertruck from Texas.

Tesla's Gigafactory Texas is the only place currently making Cybertrucks and the numbers are dwindling.

Benzinga recently shared that third-quarter delivery data showed that the most Cybertrucks sold in the third quarter could have been 8,295, with the number more likely to be under 8,000.

With annual deliveries of 28,000 to 32,000 Cybertrucks, the vehicle is not living up to Musk's original goals. The vehicle is also taking up space at the Texas factory.

JPMorgan, Coca-Cola Join Pushback Against OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Trading

JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: $JPM), Coca-Cola (NYSE: $KO), and Dell Technologies (NYSE: $DELL) and four other companies have also objected to plans by crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: $ICE) to offer tokenized versions of their shares.

An updated notice dated October 27 added JPMorgan, Coca-Cola, Dell, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: $AMD), Adobe (NASDAQ: $ADBE), Applied Materials (NASDAQ: $AMAT) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: $SNDK) to the list.

The seven companies were among the 62 firms originally notified by OKXICE, bringing the number of disclosed objections to 33, meaning about 48% of the initial roster has now objected.

More From Cryptoprowl:

Cardano Founder Hoskinson Says Midnight Will Surpass Zcash, Urges Gemini to List ADA

Stacks Founder Warns Bitcoin Security Breach Could Hit Entire Crypto Market

Coinbase Targets Banks As Institutional Crypto Adoption Grows

60 Percent of Community Banks See Stablecoins as a Threat to Deposits, Lending

Crypto Heavyweights Back OKX at $25B Valuation

The objections come amid growing caution among publicly traded companies as crypto platforms explore ways to bring traditional stocks onto blockchains.

OKXICE announced its plans on Oct. 4, proposing round-the-clock trading of tokenized US stocks through permissioned Uniswap (CRYPTO: $UNI) v4 liquidity pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain. Transactions would settle in stablecoins, including USDC (CRYPTO: $USDC).

The venue would operate under the US Securities and Exchange Commission's five-year "Innovation Exemption," which allows qualifying platforms to test blockchain-based stock trading using automated market makers.

Companies have 30 days after notification to object to the inclusion of their shares. A written objection prevents the venue from offering that company's stock, although it does not automatically exclude the shares from other platforms.

The objection list has expanded rapidly, growing from nine companies on Oct. 15 to 16 on Oct. 19 and 22 on Oct. 23. Earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Intel and Oracle.

Several major companies, including Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA), Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA), Apple (NASDAQ: $AAPL), and Amazon (NASDAQ: $AMZN), have not objected so far. Meanwhile, Nasdaq has said it will exclude its own shares from the SEC's exemption-based framework as it explores tokenized securities.
